claims.text: The as-deposited coatings are approximately 1 μm-thick FCC/BCC Al-Cr-Fe-Ni multilayers produced from Al0.2CrFeNi and Al targets.
A modulation period of 16 nm produces semicoherent FCC/BCC interfaces.
A modulation period of 8 nm produces coherent interfaces.
Modulation periods of 32 and 80 nm produce grain-boundary-dominated microstructures.
The semicoherent interfaces at 16 nm contain misfit dislocations.
Semicoherent interfaces strongly block dislocation glide.
Blocked dislocation glide causes dislocation pileup and localized high stresses at semicoherent interfaces.
Localized interfacial stresses trigger stress-induced amorphization.
The resulting amorphous interfaces have increased free volume, structural disorder, and high-energy boundaries.
Lower atomic-migration barriers enable atomic-diffusion or interface-slip creep.
Atomic diffusion or interface slip redistributes stress and enhances creep resistance.
The 16 nm coating will exhibit lower room-temperature nanoindentation creep displacement than the 8, 32, and 80 nm coatings.
The 16 nm coating will exhibit an effective creep stress exponent near 1–2.
A creep stress exponent near 1–2 indicates diffusion- or interface-slip-controlled creep.
The 8, 32, and 80 nm coatings will exhibit creep stress exponents greater than 3.
Stress exponents greater than 3 indicate dislocation-mediated creep in the comparison coatings.

The proposed behavior is limited to room-temperature nanoindentation of approximately 1 μm-thick sputtered coatings at a 5 mN maximum load and has not been extended to elevated temperatures or macroscopic loading.
Prior molecular-dynamics, HRTEM, and nanoindentation work supports stress-induced amorphization at semicoherent interfaces.

contradictions.description: The mechanism says amorphization lowers migration barriers and enables diffusion or interface slip, while the predicted outcome is reduced creep displacement and enhanced creep resistance. No intermediate rationale explains why facilitating time-dependent atomic motion should reduce rather than accelerate creep, leaving the mechanism-to-outcome direction internally unresolved.
